note: Rubric-aligned successor to v0.2. The v0.2 set is frozen and unmodified. `record_state` carries expected_verdict `supports` and is gated as its own class. `ambiguous` is rebuilt from two-sided evidence only. No challenge case ids.

relabelLedger.why: Claim asserts the record does not determine protection; cited evidence states exactly that absence. Identical evidence to J02-U14, which the set already labels does_not_establish for asserting a definite value. Reporting the blank is the mirror case.

Claim asserts the notes cannot settle current hiring. A stale first-party note and a third-party board are both non-probative for currency under the rubric, so the record genuinely fails to determine it and the claim reports that correctly.
Claim asserts uncertainty whether an eighty-day note still applies. Evidence states the note's age; stale-to-current is a never-probative inference, so the record does not determine applicability.
Claim asserts the status is unknown; evidence states the status field is blank. Direct record-state match.
Claim asserts the record does not say whether spend clears the floor; evidence states spend is unpublished.
Claim asserts authority is unresolved; evidence states a title is listed and delegation is not mentioned. Title-to-authority is never probative, so unresolved is the accurate report.
Current first-party ops and current official billing assert incompatible values of account_status. Precedence rule 3 declines to rank official above first-party, so no verdict dominates.
Claim asserts the buyer may be ready and that the note hedges; the cited note is itself hedged. The claim matches the evidence at the same strength.

Claim asserts the registry row's age is missing so currency is unclear; evidence states the row omits its age. The live v0.2 judge called this ambiguous, so this relabel moves an item away from the judge's answer.
Two comparable sources point opposite ways on hiring_freeze and both are hedged. Neither establishes nor refutes.
Claim asserts the null fact plus a passing mention leaves the matter inconclusive; evidence is exactly a passing mention with no figure. The live v0.2 judge called this ambiguous.
Claim asserts the region may be served and that it is not sure; evidence states the region is not assigned. The live v0.2 judge called this ambiguous.
Claim explicitly asserts that the evidence does not establish protection, alongside an appearance of it; a hallway comment creates exactly that appearance without establishing anything.

Claim asserts identity is unclear rather than proven; evidence states a similar trade name exists. Name-to-identity is never probative, so unproven is the accurate report. The live v0.2 judge called this ambiguous.
Claim asserts consent cannot be determined from the fragment; evidence states the inbox rule is not documented.
Claim asserts the capacity number's currency is uncertain; evidence states capacity was discussed last season with no current figure.
Newly authored two-sided item. Evidence bears on the claim from both directions with no precedence rule available; the claim contains no hedge word.
